result:
Both findings are fixed. The full e2e suite now passes in English and Arabic: 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 did not run. Nothing is committed, because the sandbox makes git read-only for this run, so the changes are waiting in the worktree for you.

**F-DG1-208 (High, mandatory): Arabic e2e journeys were red.** I went through the whole of `apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts`, not just line 138. Every role, label and text locator now has to match the whole name rather than any part of it. Where a name legitimately carries extra text, the spec now spells it out in full: nav links with their "Planned" tag, field labels with "(required)", sortable column headers, the mode radio, the filter chip and the language switch. No product strings changed.
- Full suite, both languages, real API and PostgreSQL: **22 passed, exit 0**. That includes the six Arabic journeys that were previously skipped.
- Arabic alone, using the reviewer's command: **11 passed, exit 0**.
- The accessibility scan found no violations of any severity on all 14 checked pages in each language.

**F-DG1-005 / F-DG1-008 (Low): derived-assignment audit entry was not localized.** The audit trail now shows the action as "Role granted to the creator (carried over from a business-unit assignment)" and «إسناد دور لمُنشئ السجل…» in Arabic. User, role, scope and source assignment are labelled in both languages, and the role shows as "Transformation Lead" / «قائد التحوّل» instead of `TL`. The creator's own name now comes from their session: a business-unit Lead isn't allowed to look up users, so it would otherwise show as Unknown. Anything not translated, including unknown actions, still shows raw and marked "without a translation".
- I added 6 unit tests and 3 rendered tests covering English and Arabic.
- I also added one real-stack journey: the seeded Lead creates a record and the test checks its audit trail. Screenshots in both languages are at `screenshots/{en,ar}/17-lead-audit-trail.png`. I looked at both, and the Arabic one is right-to-left.

Type check, lint, the no-CDN check, formatting, the build and all 219 unit tests (106 of them web) also pass. Nothing is blocked.

**One issue I found but didn't fix (out of scope):** right after a business-unit Lead creates a record, the page doesn't show the audit trail until it is reloaded. The browser session still holds the permissions from sign-in, which don't include the new record. The new journey reloads the page, as the reviewers' reproduction does. A likely fix is to refresh the session after a successful create, but that changes product behaviour, so it's yours to triage.

**To commit:** the 8 changed files under `apps/web/`, the handback, and its evidence folder. The dotfiles at the worktree root (`.bashrc`, `.mcp.json` and so on) aren't mine, so leave them out.

The Arabic role names that the glossary doesn't define come from the seeded role list. They still need review by a Mobily Arabic-language owner.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG1/round-3/`:
- `T-DG1-FE4-frontend-ux-engineer.md`
- `T-DG1-FE4-evidence/` (logs, screenshots, `changes.diff`)
